title: Adversarial Structural Security Intelligence (ASSI): Research Foundation
description:
Adversarial Structural Security Intelligence (ASSI) is a specification-first research foundation investigating structural security beyond cryptographic validity. It develops research hypotheses, conceptual architectures, and proposed contracts for compositional identity and Universal Trigger Nodes (UTN), directional weak-evidence reasoning and Relational Evidence Navigation (REN), Bidirectional Conditional Evidence Feedback (BCEF), independently governed authorization, adversarial security drives, security residuals, autonomous questioning, and validated recursive self-improvement.

Version 0.1.0 comprises twelve core research papers, six draft specifications, five conceptual cases, four extensions, and research-navigation and validation-planning documents. It proposes four benchmark families for future controlled, synthetic experiments; these benchmarks are plans, not completed empirical results. The repository does not claim a working security product, independent validation, production readiness, certification, or a demonstrated security guarantee.

Key separation principles: inference is not authority; simulation is not validation; validation is not deployment approval. The project is intended to support transparent critique, falsifiable research, and collective learning.
notes: Research foundation only. The proposed benchmarks and validation roadmap do not constitute completed experiments or security certification. Verify attribution and repository URL before release.
